findings.claim: Removing the isHighFrequencyAguiEvent filter means every validated official frame — including each per-token TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT/REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT delta — now upserts a RuntimeAgUiEvent entity into the zustand graph store once per token, reintroducing the per-token store-update churn and unbounded entity growth the deleted filter was deliberately preventing.
findings.evidence: Deleted code: `if (!isHighFrequencyAguiEvent(event)) { ingestAgUiEvent(...) }` with comment 'High-frequency token deltas are excluded to keep the AG-UI events panel readable.' Replacement: `if (adapted.eventRow) ingestAgUiEvent(runId, adapted.eventRow);` with comment 'including high-frequency content rows.' runtime-ingest.ts upserts one entity per row.id with no eviction or cap, so a long stream produces one graph-store entity (and subscriber notification) per streamed token.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap or coalesce RuntimeAgUiEvent ingestion for delta-type rows (e.g., keep only the latest N rows per run, or upsert deltas into a single rolling 'latest content' entity) while retaining full rows for lifecycle/tool/state events.

findings.claim: The added allow entry `Bash(gh secret *)` grants non-interactive permission to run any gh secret subcommand (list, set, delete) against the repository's CI credentials, broadening agent capability over production secrets with no ask-gate.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk adds `"Bash(gh secret *)"` to the permissions allow array, alongside other write-capable entries; the file's `ask` array remains empty (`"ask": []`), so nothing forces confirmation before secret mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the permission to read-only forms (e.g., `Bash(gh secret list)`) and leave `gh secret set/delete` unprompted-by-default via the `ask` list or explicit operator invocation.
